 Dated this the 16th day of February, 2024  ORDER
Petitioner is the first accused in C.C.No.1027/2023 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kodungallur.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kodungallur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The case arises out of Crime No.662/2023 of Kodungallur Police Station.
2. Though petitioner had approached this Court in Crl.M.C. No.9611 of 2023, by order dated 15.11.2023, this Court relegated the petitioner to approach the Trial Court through a discharge petition.
Thereafter, Crl.M.P. No.8212/2023 was filed by the petitioner, and by the impugned order dated 16.01.2024, the learned Magistrate dismissed the discharge petition.
This Crl.M.C. is filed against the said order of discharge.

3. According to the prosecution, the accused had, promised to provide Visa and employment to the defacto complainant and five others in a hotel at Malta and collected their passports and a large amount of money from them and later, failed to provide the employment or return the money and the passports and thereby they had fraudulently induced the defacto complainant and other witnesses to part with their property and committing the offences under Sections 406 and 420 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
4.

The learned Magistrate, by the impugned order, held that the accused had failed to fulfill a promise and even refused to return the money and that prima facie materials were available to show that the accused had acted in furtherance of their common intention to defraud the witnesses and cheated CWs2 to 6 under the promise to secure a visa.

It was also held that the records were sufficient to proceed with the trial of the case and also that the case cannot be said to be a mere breach of contract or a civil dispute and the prosecution records prima facie showed that there was inducement and promise, and that the amount was collected based on those promises and hence,
the accused is not entitled for a discharge.
5.

Sri. Prabhu K N, the learned counsel for the petitioner contended that though revisional jurisdiction is available against the impugned order, remedy under Section 482 Cr.P.C. can be resorted to, as held by the Supreme Court in Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Pvt. Ltd.

entities.text: Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: And Another v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2018 (16) SCC 299].

entities.text: Another v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2018 (16) SCC 299]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was further submitted that Annexure-A3 civil suit is pending before the Munsiff Court, Kodungallur, and the dispute is a pure civil dispute which is attempted to be camouflaged as a criminal case and therefore, the accused ought to be discharged.

The learned counsel further referred to the employment agreement handed over by the accused indicating that the promise had been partially complied with and what remained was only a breach of contract for which the remedy is before the Civil Court.

6. Sri. Noushad K. A, the learned Public Prosecutor submitted that the learned Magistrate had, while considering the discharge petition referred to the prima facie case against the accused and had also Shanil Stephen V vs State Of Kerala on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199913660/
2 held that there was sufficient material to proceed with the trial of the case.

entities.text: Shanil Stephen V vs State Of Kerala on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Public Prosecutor also pointed out that the passport and the money collected by the petitioner and the other accused had not been returned till date, and sufficient materials have been collected by the Investigating Officer to mulct a criminal liability on the accused.
7. I have considered the rival contentions.

8. In Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Pvt. Ltd.' s Case (Supra), Supreme Court held that the challenge against an order of discharge can be entertained by the High Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C only in rarest of rare cases, to correct patent errors of jurisdiction and not to re-appreciate the matter.

entities.text: Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Though the power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C is wide, as observed by the Supreme Court, when an order of discharge is challenged, the normal remedy is before the revisional court.
However, in exceptional circumstances, the parties are entitled to approach the High Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.

On a perusal of the circumstances arising in the case and the materials produced, this Court finds no such exceptional circumstances to exercise jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
9.
However, since the learned counsel for the petitioner insisted that the jurisdiction is available, I have heard the counsel and considered the matter on merits itself.

10. A perusal of the final report reveals that the accused had collected a large amount of money from six persons, promising them to provide employment in a hotel at Malta and collected their passports.
Neither the passport nor the amount has been returned till date.

Though an agreement was handed over by the accused to the Investigating Officer indicating an employer acceptance contract, it is seen not evident whether those were handed over to the defacto complainant or the other witnesses nor were they issued with any Visa.

It is seen from the statement of the witnesses produced before this Court that they have narrated the circumstances under which they were taken to Delhi with the promise of being issued with Visa and thereafter, they returned back after waiting for several days without the Visa or passport or even the money.
11. Prima facie I am satisfied that, sufficient materials are available to proceed with the offences alleged against the petitioner.

This is not a fit case where the accused could be discharged,
considering the materials collected by the prosecution.
The impugned order is therefore proper and regular.

Accordingly, I find no merits in this criminal miscellaneous case and it is dismissed.
Sd/-
BECHU KURIAN THOMAS JUDGE Jka/16.02.24.
